key_insight: For shape-informed hemodynamic surrogates, active learning and finite-element physical consistency are most effective during fine-tuning, while out-of-distribution performance is chiefly limited by geometric coverage.
engineering_relevance: The workflow supports scalable prediction of patient-specific aortic velocity and pressure fields toward real-time cardiovascular assessment.
method: Generate physiologically consistent CFD solutions on SynthAorta geometries using automatic boundary-condition adjustment.
Represent anatomy through displacement fields from a common reference and predict peak-systolic flow with Graph U-Net and Transformer U-Net models.
Fine-tune using active learning and differentiable finite-element residual constraints.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparisons of sampling and physics-constraint strategies across training stages, plus out-of-distribution tests, but provides no numerical accuracy or speedup results.
watch_item: Generalization to anatomies outside the geometric parametrization remains a limitation that architecture changes alone may not resolve.
paper_title: Synthetic Dataset Generation, Physical Consistency and Active Learning for Shape-Informed Surrogate Modeling of Hemodynamics
